record.original_question: For a classical solution of the kinetic equation f_t + v · grad_x f = a_ij(t, x, v) partial_{v_i v_j} f on [0, 1] x B_1 x B_1 with uniformly elliptic coefficients lambda I <= {a_ij} <= Lambda I, does a Krylov-Safonov-type interior Holder estimate hold? In other words, must there exist alpha > 0 and C, depending only on dimension and ellipticity, such that ||f||_{C^alpha((1/2, 1) x B_{1/2} x B_{1/2})} <= C ||f||_{L^infinity([0, 1] x B_1 x B_1)}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.1. Assume f : [0, 1] × B1 × B1 → R is a (classical) solution of an equation of the following form ft + v · ∇x f = aij (t, x, v)∂vi vj f.
Then, there exists constants α > 0 and C, depending only on dimension and the ellipticity parameters λ and Λ, so that kf kC α((1/2,1)×B1/2 ×B1/2 ) ≤ Ckf kL∞ ([0,1]×B1 ×B1 ) .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 1$, and let $\lambda,\Lambda>0$ be fixed ellipticity constants. Suppose $f:[0,1]\times B_1\times B_1\to\mathbb{R}$ is a classical solution of the kinetic equation
$$\partial_t f + v\cdot\nabla_x f \;=\; a_{ij}(t,x,v)\,\partial_{v_i v_j} f \quad\text{on } [0,1]\times B_1\times B_1,$$
where $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denotes the open unit ball, $(a_{ij}(t,x,v))$ is a symmetric matrix-valued function that is merely measurable in $(t,x,v)$, and satisfies the uniform ellipticity condition
$$\lambda\, I \;\leq\; (a_{ij}(t,x,v)) \;\leq\; \Lambda\, I \qquad\text{for almost every } (t,x,v).$$
Decide whether there exist constants $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $C>0$, depending only on the dimension $n$ and on $\lambda,\Lambda$, such that for every such solution $f$ one has the interior Hölder estimate
$$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha}\bigl((1/2,1)\times B_{1/2}\times B_{1/2}\bigr)} \;\leq\; C\,\|f\|_{L^{\infty}([0,1]\times B_1\times B_1)}.$$
Here $C^\alpha$ is taken with respect to a kinetic (Galilean-invariant) distance, or equivalently one asks for Hölder continuity separately in each of the variables $t$, $x$, and $v$ with some positive exponent depending only on $n,\lambda,\Lambda$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is the non-divergence (Krylov–Safonov-type) analogue of the kinetic De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theorem. Recent literature treats only the divergence-form case (Golse–Imbert–Mouhot–Vasseur and subsequent works) or assumes regularity of coefficients (e.g., Schauder estimates by Imbert–Silvestre, Biagi–Bramanti). No proof of a Krylov–Safonov-type Hölder estimate for kinetic equations in non-divergence form with merely bounded measurable coefficients has been found in the literature, and it is stated as an open problem in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Schauder estimates on bounded domains for KFP operators (Biagi–Bramanti, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Considers KFP operators with coefficients Hölder continuous in space; assumes coefficient regularity rather than only measurability.
status_evidence.claim: Recent non-divergence kinetic regularity results require Hölder coefficients, not merely measurable.

status_evidence.title: Hölder estimates for kinetic Fokker-Planck equations up to the boundary (arXiv:2206.12387)
status_evidence.snippet: De Giorgi/Moser-type Hölder regularity for kinetic Fokker–Planck equations in divergence form with rough coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Available rough-coefficient kinetic Hölder results are in divergence form, not the non-divergence Krylov–Safonov setting.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to fully nonlinear parabolic equations (Imbert–Silvestre)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Krylov–Safonov theory; kinetic non-divergence version remains a target conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The kinetic Krylov–Safonov estimate is identified as an open conjecture.
